edition.locus: Eusebius HE 5.1.24-28 (Sanctus restored; Biblias reclaims her crown)

source_text: Ἐπεὶ γὰρ ἀνόμως μεθ᾽ ἡμέρας πάλιν στρεβλοῦντες τὸν μάρτυρα καὶ νομίζοντες ὅτι οἰδούντων καὶ φλεγμαινόντων τῶν σωμάτων εἰ τὰ αὐτὰ προσενέχοιεν κολαστήρια, περιέσοιντο αὐτοῦ, ὁπότε οὐδὲ τὴν ἀπὸ τῶν χειρῶν ἁφὴν ἠνείχετο, ἢ ὅτε ἐναποθανὼν ταῖς βασάνοις φόβον ἐμποιήσειεν τοῖς λοιποῖς, οὐ μόνον οὐδὲν περὶ αὐτὸν τοιοῦτο συνέβη, ἀλλὰ καὶ παρὰ πᾶσαν δόξαν ἀνθρώπων ἀνέστη καὶ ἀνωρθώθη τὸ σωμάτιον ἐν ταῖς μετέπειτα βασάνοις, καὶ τὴν ἰδέαν ἀπέλαβεν τὴν προτέραν καὶ τὴν χρῆσιν τῶν μελῶν, ὥστε μὴ κόλασιν, ἀλλ᾽ ἴασιν διὰ τῆς χάριτος τοῦ Χριστοῦ τὴν δευτέραν στρέβλωσιν αὐτῷ γενέσθαι. Καὶ Βιβλίδα δέ, μίαν τῶν ἠρνημένων, ἤδη δοκῶν ὁ διάβολος καταπεπωκέναι, θελήσας δὲ καὶ διὰ βλασφημίας κατακρῖναι, ἦγεν ἐπὶ κόλασιν, ἀναγκάζων εἰπεῖν τὰ ἄθεα περὶ ἡμῶν, ὡς εὔθραυστον ἤδη καὶ ἄνανδρον· ἡ δὲ ἐν τῇ στρεβλώσει ἀνένηψεν καὶ ὡς ἂν εἴπειν ἐκ βαθέος ὕπνου ἀνεγρηγόρησεν, ὑπομνησθεῖσα διὰ τῆς προσκαίρου τιμωρίας τὴν αἰώνιον ἐν γεέννῃ κόλασιν, καὶ ἐξ ἐναντίας ἀντεῖπεν τοῖς βλασφήμοις, φήσασα· Πῶς ἂν παιδία φάγοιεν οἱ τοιοῦτοι, οἷς μηδὲ ἀλόγων ζῴων αἷμα φαγεῖν ἐξόν; Καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦδε Χριστιανὴν ἑαυτὴν ὡμολόγει καὶ τῷ κλήρῳ τῶν μαρτύρων προσετέθη.
pass_a_gloss: For since lawlessly after days again racking the witness and supposing that, with the bodies swollen and inflamed, if they should apply the same instruments of punishment they would get the better of him, since he did not even endure touch from hands, or that dying under the tortures he would put fear into the rest, not only did nothing of that sort happen concerning him, but also contrary to all human expectation he stood up and the little body was set upright in the later tortures, and it received back its former appearance and the use of its limbs, so that the second twisting became for him not punishment but healing through the grace of Christ. And Biblis also, one of those who had denied, whom the devil supposed he had already swallowed down, and wishing to condemn her also through blasphemy, he led to punishment, compelling her to say the godless things about us, as being already fragile and unmanly; but she in the twisting came to herself and, as one might say, was awakened out of deep sleep, having been reminded by the temporary penalty of the eternal punishment in Gehenna, and on the contrary spoke against the blasphemers, saying: How would such people eat children, to whom it is not permitted even to eat blood of irrational animals? And from that point she confessed herself a Christian and was added to the lot of the martyrs.
pass_b_english: For after an interval of days they again put the witness to the rack in lawless fashion, supposing that, now that his frame was swollen and inflamed, if they applied the same engines they would break him, since he could not even bear the touch of hands, or else that by dying under the tortures he would strike fear into the rest. Yet not only did none of this happen to him, but beyond all human expectation he rose and his poor little body was set upright amid the later tortures, and recovered its former shape and the use of its limbs, so that the second racking became for him through the grace of Christ not torment but healing.

And as for Biblias, one of those who had denied, whom the devil thought he had already swallowed down (First Peter 5:8) and wished to condemn besides through blasphemy, he brought her to torment, forcing her, as one already frail and cowardly, to speak the godless charges against us. But in the midst of the racking she came to herself and, so to speak, awoke out of deep sleep, reminded by the short-lived penalty of the eternal punishment in Gehenna (Matthew 25:46), and answered the blasphemers back to their faces, saying: How could such people eat children, when it is not even permitted them to eat the blood of brute beasts (Acts 15:29)? And from that hour she confessed herself a Christian and was numbered with the company of the martyrs.

lemmas.gloss: would get the better of, would overcome him

choices.english: in lawless fashion, after an interval of days, again
choices.why: ἀνόμως is adverbial manner and μεθ᾽ ἡμέρας marks elapsed time before renewed torture, while πάλιν repeats the action rather than merely continuing it.
diminutive -ιον here conveys pitiable smallness after swelling and inflammation, not neutral anatomy, matching ἀνέστη and ἀνωρθώθη of a ruined frame.

choices.term: μὴ κόλασιν, ἀλλ᾽ ἴασιν ... τὴν δευτέραν στρέβλωσιν αὐτῷ γενέσθαι
choices.english: the second racking became for him not torment but healing
choices.why: μὴ ... ἀλλά contrasts outcome, and γενέσθαι with dative αὐτῷ marks what the torture turned into for him, with χάριτος τοῦ Χριστοῦ as instrumental cause.
rejected: the second twisting did not punish but healed him

choices.english: Biblis, one of those who had denied
choices.why: μίαν with genitive τῶν ἠρνημένων is partitive and perfect in sense, denoting prior denial before this renewed examination, not general unbelief.
